quotes.text: A copilot skill is a reusable instruction set for AI. Think of it like writing a job description for a temporary worker.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a crisp, memorable definition of a Copilot skill.

quotes.text: A skill is not a chatbot that you sit and talk to. It's a specialist that only activates when needed.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Corrects the common misconception that skills are chatbots.

quotes.text: Use skills for repeatable expertise, tasks where the AI needs to think and adapt. Use workflows for strict order and approvals. Tasks where you can't afford variation.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear decision rule between skills and workflows.

quotes.text: Don't create two skills with similar names or overlapping triggers. If you have a meeting notes skill and a meeting summary skill sitting side by side, co-pilot won't know which one to use.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical design advice for keeping a skill library unambiguous.

quotes.text: Skills are called on demand. They're not always active. Every time the skill runs, it burns AI processing. So keep your instructions short and focused.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why concise skill instructions save processing and cost.

chapters.title: Creating a skill with Agent Builder

takeaways: A Copilot skill is a reusable instruction set made of a name, a trigger description and step-by-step instructions that runs only when a request matches.
Skills live in three homes: Agent Builder in Copilot Chat for no-code creation, Copilot Studio for Markdown files with scripts, and Copilot Cowork for skill files in OneDrive.
Good skills have precise names, specific triggers, short instructions, a defined output format and explicit rules, and they improve through testing and iteration.
hook: Microsoft calls the same idea agents in one product and skills in another, which leaves many Copilot users confused. This episode explains in plain English what a Copilot skill is, where it lives in Copilot Chat, Copilot Studio and Copilot Cowork, and how beginners can build their first reliable, reusable skill.
